structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E033. Tip E033: 8.75 true epochs, 219 steps, 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%. It runs 5.691 s and scores 0.7536 on seeds 0–2. Its held-out mean passed the 0.752 gate, so it is probably about 0.752–0.754.

1. Settled by reading the code:
- Muon has no wd, and the filters are renormalized every step. All wd effects come from the SGD groups.
- Newton-Schulz already runs 3 steps.
- Images already travel as uint8 and are normalized on the GPU.
- The whitening-bias lr goes to 0 at 3 epochs (about 34% of steps), but its backward keeps running.
- prepare's eigh/cusolver, pad and randperm are never warmed in build. That is the likely source of trial 0's extra ~0.15 s.

2. Chaotic decorrelation (E029, E030, E032). Any change to the dynamics re-rolls the per-seed outcomes. The result is then about 0.7525 plus the idea's true effect, with a 3-seed SD of about 0.15 pp. Time-neutral boosters on top of the airbench schedule have a mean effect of 0 to −0.4 pp: the schedule sits at a sharp optimum, while the weight knobs are flat. I now also expect "neutral" structural changes to cost about 0.1 pp on average, not 0.

3. Time model, corrected after five low-side misses. Steps at large maps cost more than their MAC share. E028: freezing group 1 for 25% of steps saved 0.84 s. E031: removing 20 steps saved 0.95 s. E033: moving 15% of steps from 24 to 20 px saved 0.19 s, more than the pixel ratio predicts. My mechanism: on 31×31/23×23 maps, the BN/GELU/pool forward and backward are bandwidth-bound and scale super-linearly with map area. On top of that there is a fixed per-step host/optimizer cost (eager fused SGD, a separate Muon graph, Python LR loops, Lookahead foreach on 4 CPUs), roughly 5–8 ms per step. So step removal and stem truncation pay about 1.5× what MAC models say. I bias time forecasts low.

4. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The jump into 32 px and the length of the 28/32 tail carry the accuracy (E011, E018, E024).

5. Dials:
- Epochs: 0.25 epoch ≈ 0.13 s ≈ 0.12 pp.
- Freeze: about 0.8 s for about 0.2 pp. That is about 3× better than the epoch dial, so freeze + epoch top-up is the main path, at about 5.2 s.
- Freeze dose beyond 25%: probably costs accuracy faster, because group-1 features at 28 px have not yet adapted to 32 px.

6. Noise:
- 3-seed mean: SD about 0.15 pp.
- 10-seed held-out mean: SE about 0.08 pp.
- Rebuild drift: 0.03–0.05 pp.
- Seeds 3–12 carry a winner's curse after about 11 keep decisions. I expect fresh seeds to come in about 0.1 pp below them.

Unsure:
- Host overhead vs bandwidth as the source of the excess savings. If it is host overhead, capturing the optimizer and Lookahead inside one graph is the next systems lever nobody has proposed.
- Transfer to the PCIe judge for bandwidth-bound levers.
- Whether a held-out mean of about 0.753 survives 40 seeds. I think it likely does.

forecasts.reason: The time half (≤5.75) is near-certain, since the freeze saves ~0.8 s and +0.5 epoch adds ~0.28 s. Held-out ≥0.7540 is a coin flip: the freeze's −0.2 pp versus the epochs' +0.24 pp, under a re-roll.
Part 1 is already in the code. Warming eigh/cusolver and pad in build removes most of trial 0's ~0.15 s, so the mean drops by about 0.05 s, with bit-identical accuracy.
Removing the whitening GELU backward and conv1 dgrad on 31×31 maps over 80% of steps is bandwidth-heavy, so it likely saves ≥2%. The accuracy is a re-roll, and the ≤0.1 pp test cannot be resolved.
Freezing group 1 before it has adapted to 32 px costs accuracy faster than the dose increase. The time saving is likely ≥3%, but the held-out loss is likely >0.15 pp.
It is a diagnostic, so seeds 0–2 are unchanged. I expect fresh seeds 13–22 about 0.1 pp below 3–12 because of the winner's curse, which leaves the pooled mean near 0.7525–0.753, right at the bar.
The frozen phase already skips backward. Folding removes only the forward BN reductions on 25% of steps, about 0.05–0.08 s, which is under 2%.
I expect non-GEMM kernels to take ≥30% of the step, and the stem plus group 1 to take ≥35% at 32 px, consistent with E028's excess saving.
With 219 steps at batch 2000, SGD loses its per-step efficiency, so the held-out mean drops ≥0.3 pp. Removing Newton-Schulz saves about 3% of time.

cruxes: Is the excess saving from step removal and stem truncation (E028, E031, E033) host/optimizer overhead per step, or large-map memory bandwidth? If host overhead, capturing the SGD, Muon and Lookahead updates in one CUDA graph is a ~5–10% lever nobody has tried.
On fresh seeds 13–22, does the tip's mean stay ≥0.7525, or does the winner's curse push it toward 0.751? That decides whether the freeze + epoch path must buy extra margin.
On held-out seeds, is the freeze's accuracy cost about 0.1 pp or about 0.3 pp? That sets whether I052 at 9.25 epochs clears the gate, or whether 9.5 epochs is needed.
